AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Radical nephrectomy (RN) and caval thrombectomy (CT) for renal cell carcinoma, with extracorporeal circulation (ECC) and deep hypothermic circulatory arrest (DHCA) is a challenging surgical approach.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To assess peri-operative and oncologic outcomes of renal cell carcinoma patients treated with RN and CT, using ECC and DHCA.

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS
AbstractText.content: We retrospectively evaluated 46 patients who underwent RN and CT using ECC and DHCA.

AbstractText.Label: SURGICAL PROCEDURE
AbstractText.content: After retroperitoneal nodal dissection and RN, a cardiopulmonary bypass was placed and DHCA achieved. A combined approach through the abdomen and the thorax was described.

AbstractText.Label: MEASUREMENTS
AbstractText.content: Perioperative and long-term survival outcomes were reported.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS AND LIMITATIONS
AbstractText.content: Median operative time and length of hospital stay were 545min and 22 d. Overall, 33 patients (72%) did not require any additional interventional or surgical treatment. Thirty-day and 90-d mortality were 11% (5/46) and 15% (7/46). The 1-yr, 2-yr, and 3-yr cancer specific mortality (CSM)-free survival rates were 77%, 62%, and 56%, respectively. After stratification, according to metastatic status at diagnosis, CSM-free survival rates were significantly lower for cM1 patients compared with cM0 patients (1-yr 46% vs 93%, 2-yr 23% vs 81%, 3-yr 23% vs 73%, p<0.01). Our study is limited by its retrospective and uncomparative nature.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: RN with CT using ECC and DHCA is a challenging procedure which requires a dedicated multidisciplinary working team to minimise complications and maximise patients' outcomes.

AbstractText.Label: PATIENT SUMMARY
AbstractText.content: Patients with kidney cancer and a thrombus within the inferior vena cava, which reaches above the diaphragm, can be treated with surgery. However, this kind of surgical treatment is challenging and requires a dedicated multidisciplinary team in order to accomplish the task.
